symptom:
A doc comment line starting with a markdown `*` bullet lost its marker on describe → exec, one marker per cycle: `describe entity` printed `/**
 * Intro line
* bullet one
 */` and the replay stored `bullet one` (mendixlabs/mxcli#1428, 1 of 155 rows in the banking round trip).
cause:
The describer side, not the parser: eleven describers (entity, association, enumeration, image collection, queue, regular expression, scheduled event and the four agent-editor doctypes) printed documentation with `"/**
 * %s
 */
"`, which gutters the first line only, and the entity attribute used the inline `/** %s */`. extractDocComment strips exactly one leading `*` per line, so an unguttered `* bullet` line lost its marker. The describers that split on newlines (microflow, page, constant, mappings, module, menu, Java action) were already right.
file: mdl/executor/cmd_entities_describe.go (entity + attribute), cmd_associations.go, cmd_enumerations.go, cmd_imagecollections.go, cmd_queues.go, cmd_regularexpressions.go, cmd_scheduledevents.go, cmd_agenteditor_{agents,kbs,mcpservices,models}.go — all now call outputJavadocIndented (cmd_odata.go)
insight: Pick the side by asking which one is wrong for a value it can see: the parser's one-`*`-per-line rule is the javadoc convention and correct for a guttered block, so the describer that omits the gutter is the defect. A single-line `/** %s */` is only safe for one line not itself starting with `*` — `/** * x */` loses the marker the same way. The bug survived because describe of a one-line doc looks right; only a multi-line doc whose continuation starts with `*` shows it, and without the `*` the unguttered line was silently tolerated (the parser trims whitespace), so the copy-paste format string spread to eleven files. Grep `/\*\*\\n \* %s` for the copy. Verified: three describe → check → exec-on-a-fresh-copy cycles on an 11.6.6 app print byte-identical output, mx check 0 errors.
